text.p: Marling Industries Plc said on Monday that a delay at its unit VOAC/SW will have an adverse effect on the second six months, and consequently, on the group's results for the year ending March 31, 1997.
However, Marling said results for the six months ended September 30, 1996, remained in line with expectations and added that it would remain profitable in the second half.

It said that the expansion of its industrial webbing plant in Canada was now complete but the process had taken longer than expected and had delayed the certification of VOAC/SW's webbing while bulk production runs had not yet started.
VOAC/SW is Marling's North American unit following the purchase of Woven Electronics Corp's seat belting business, Southern Weaving.
Marling said VOAC/SW should break even in the year ending March 31, 1998 and generate profits thereafter.
It has also taken steps to strengthen the management at VOAC/SW and now anticipates that final certifications will be received before the end of the calendar year.
Marling also said that with the exception of its German healthcare business Muller, its other businesses continue to perform in line with expectations.
Pre-production testing of the new Muller antithrombosis stocking has taken longer than expected, said Marling.
Marling shares were down 3-1/4p to 14-1/2p at 0740 GMT.
